gpu_backend_loading.mechanism: ggml-base.dll dynamically loads ggml-<backend>.dll. llama.cpp official builds do not set GGML_BACKEND_DIR, so the search order is the executable's own directory, then the current working directory; GGML_BACKEND_PATH is the only override.
gpu_backend_loading.consequence: ggml-cuda.dll must be copied into runtime/windows (next to jev-score.exe). Putting it on PATH does nothing.
gpu_backend_loading.exe_dependency_check: jev-score.exe and jev-score-v2.exe import only KERNEL32/api-ms-win-crt-*, ggml-base.dll, ggml.dll, llama.dll. GPU support is never compiled into the EXE; it comes from the backend DLL.

rtx_5060_laptop.compute_capability: sm_120 (Blackwell) - not measured on this machine, taken from llama.cpp arch table
why_gpu_is_ignored: the bundled CUDA backend is the CUDA 12.4 build: its ggml-cuda.dll imports cudart64_12.dll/cublas64_12.dll/cublasLt64_12.dll, which a CUDA 13.3 install does not provide
that build contains device code only for sm_50..sm_90, so it has no kernels for sm_120 (llama.cpp requires CUDA >= 12.8 for Blackwell)
ggml-cuda.dll must sit in the same directory as jev-score.exe (or the CWD, or GGML_BACKEND_PATH); being on PATH is not enough
